[{"content": ""You are a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield, where the five departments under review total 596 authorized positions (542 filled): Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, and Fire Department. The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

- NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv


External reference snapshots are provided in task_folder/references/ when the task requires external sources. Use these pinned files; internet access is unavailable. Write requested deliverables in /work/output/.

[{"content": ""You are a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield, where the five departments under review total 596 authorized positions (542 filled): Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, and Fire Department. The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

[{"content": ""You are a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield, where the five departments under review total 596 authorized positions (542 filled): Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, and Fire Department. The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

Local Reference Files:
- Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv
- Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx
- NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv


External reference snapshots are provided in task_folder/references/ when the task requires external sources. Use these pinned files; internet access is unavailable. Write requested deliverables in /work/output/.

The data included in the MMRs provide valuable
transparency on demand for public services and

Although MMR data does not explicitly identify
funding or staff associated with the performance
indicators, it provides important details to link
spending and staffing to agency performance

associated with a service. In November 2023,
OSC released its Agency Services Monitoring

expense data that is regularly provided by the

fiscal and performance data is valuable to fully
understand the underlying causes of the staffing
challenges.
The City’s response to these ongoing challenges
will have important fiscal implications.
Corresponding with these staffing challenges and
the post-pandemic rebound in service demand,
some agencies have increased their reliance on
overtime to meet their short-term staffing needs.
If a shortage remains unaddressed, in certain
cases, the City may also be at risk of future
litigation for noncompliance with legal or
contractual mandates. The City should continue
to make efforts to properly target staffing levels to
meet necessary demand and focus hiring efforts
on ensuring City services are meeting the
standards of quality it has set for serving
residents.

The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A ("Consolidate") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into "Community Wellness" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into "Public Works," with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B ("Targeted Fix") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. "Baseline Metrics" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. "Proposal A Model" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. "Proposal B Model" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. "Comparison Summary" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

"Baseline Metrics" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. "Proposal A Model" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. "Proposal B Model" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. "Comparison Summary" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's "2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

- **FDNY**: Avg response time structural fires 4:37 vs target 4:14; avg response time life-threatening medical emergencies 9:32 vs target 6:55 (missed); ambulance turnaround 40:03

Also DPR cleanliness ratings at community district level — let me check whether those have any accepted values (any year), since park cleanliness is a great analog to Greenfield park maintenance. Also check historical values for these key indicators (e.g., DOT pothole %, DOHMH birth cert, FDNY response times across FY16-FY26) to give trend context.

Then extract the NYC budget CSV to compute per-employee budget for the five NYC agencies (need headcounts — which may come from the Comptroller report or the budget CSV itself). Let me check what agencies/units are in NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv.

The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

[{"content": ""You are a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield, where the five departments under review total 596 authorized positions (542 filled): Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, and Fire Department. The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

Local Reference Files:
- Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv
- Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx
- NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv


External reference snapshots are provided in task_folder/references/ when the task requires external sources. Use these pinned files; internet access is unavailable. Write requested deliverables in /work/output/.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

- Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx
- NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv


External reference snapshots are provided in task_folder/references/ when the task requires external sources. Use these pinned files; internet access is unavailable. Write requested deliverables in /work/output/.

[{"content": ""You are a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield, where the five departments under review total 596 authorized positions (542 filled): Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, and Fire Department. The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

- NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv


External reference snapshots are provided in task_folder/references/ when the task requires external sources. Use these pinned files; internet access is unavailable. Write requested deliverables in /work/output/.

- Parks & Rec: 116 auth, 110 filled, 5.2% vacancy
- Sanitation: 108 auth, 101 filled, 6.5% vacancy
- Transportation: 134 auth, 114 filled, 14.9% vacancy, turnover 20%

**Overtime (FY2024 annual):**
- Fire: $2,085,312 OT (14.57% of regular hours) — TRIGGERS Proposal B's >10% OT
- Health: $525,390 (7.13%)
- Parks: $453,960 (6.05%)
- Sanitation: $646,877 (9.79%)
- Transportation: $642,979 (8.36%)
- Total OT: $4,354,518; OT hours 109,442; regular hours 1,141,177

Note: only Fire exceeds the 10% OT threshold on an annual basis. But Sanitation exceeded 10% in several months (Nov 10.0, Dec 13.5, Jan 14.4, Feb 12.7...). Let me check which months exceeded 10% for each dept — Sanitation crosses 10% in winter months. I should check full monthly pivot. In Proposal B, "shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours" — on annual basis, Fire (14.6%) triggers; Sanitation is at 9.8% annual (borderline, spikes in winter). I can note this.

**Process metrics:**
- Worst on-time per dept: Fire 59.6% (Plan Review), Health 64.1% (Env Complaint), Parks 62.4% (Tree Removal), Sanitation 54.2% (Illegal Dumping), Transportation 48.3% (Street Resurfacing)
- 8 processes below 65% on-time: Transportation has 3 (worst), Sanitation 2, Parks 1, Health 1, Fire 1
- Volume-weighted cycle times: Transportation 7.90 days (worst), Fire 3.78, Parks 4.28, Health 1.80, Sanitation 1.06

**311 data** (500 requests FY2024):
- DSNY (Sanitation): 148 requests, 9.05 avg days, 3.64 satisfaction
- DOT (Transportation): 126 requests, 13.62 avg days, 3.36 satisfaction (lowest)
- DPR (Parks): 99, 12.50 days, 3.55
- DHS (Health): 75, 12.00 days, 3.72
- FDNY (Fire): 52, 3.82 days, 4.23 (best)
- 437 closed (87.4%), 63 open/in-progress

Now, the "average 311 resolution days" per department for the Baseline Metrics tab: use the closed-request average resolution days by department.

Wait — the mapping: Greenfield 311 uses DHS for Health Services. Hmm, DHS is usually Homeless Services, but given the Greenfield departments are Parks, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, Fire — the five 311 codes DPR, DSNY, DOT, DHS, FDNY map 1:1 to them. I'll note that DHS here = Health Services (the dataset's coding). Good.

Now let me analyze the NYC MMR data and the NYC budget CSV, then the Comptroller PDF.

The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

"Baseline Metrics" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. "Proposal A Model" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. "Proposal B Model" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. "Comparison Summary" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's "2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

{"command": "cd /work && python3 << 'EOF'
import pandas as pd, openpyxl

wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('task_folder/Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx', data_only=True)
def sheet_df(name):
    vals = list(wb[name].values)
    return pd.DataFrame(vals[1:], columns=vals[0])

ss = sheet_df('Staffing_Summary')
for c_ in ['Authorized_Positions','Filled_Positions','Vacancy_Rate_Pct','Avg_Tenure_Years','Turnover_Rate_Pct','Avg_Annual_Salary']:
    ss[c_] = pd.to_numeric(ss[c_])

tot_auth, tot_fill = ss['Authorized_Positions'].sum(), ss['Filled_Positions'].sum()
print(f"Total authorized: {tot_auth}, filled: {tot_fill}, vacancies: {tot_auth-tot_fill}, citywide vacancy: {100*(tot_auth-tot_fill)/tot_auth:.1f}%")
d = ss.groupby('Department').agg(auth=('Authorized_Positions','sum'), filled=('Filled_Positions','sum'), vac_rate=('Vacancy_Rate_Pct','mean'), turnover=('Turnover_Rate_Pct','mean'), salary=('Avg_Annual_Salary','mean'))
d['vac_calc'] = 100*(d['auth']-d['filled'])/d['auth']
print(d.round(1).to_string())

mo = sheet_df('Monthly_Overtime')
for c_ in ['Regular_Hours','Overtime_Hours','Overtime_Cost_USD','OT_as_Pct_of_Regular']:
    mo[c_] = pd.to_numeric(mo[c_])
print("\n=== OT ANNUAL BY DEPT ===")
ot = mo.groupby('Department').agg(reg=('Regular_Hours','sum'), ot_h=('Overtime_Hours','sum'), ot_cost=('Overtime_Cost_USD','sum'), avg_pct=('OT_as_Pct_of_Regular','mean'))
ot['pct_calc'] = 100*ot['ot_h']/ot['reg']
ot['avg_hr_rate'] = ot['ot_cost']/ot['ot_h']
print(ot.round(2).to_string())
print("\nTotal OT cost:", round(ot['ot_cost'].sum(),0), "| reg hrs:", ot['reg'].sum(), "| OT hrs:", ot['ot_h'].sum())

pmx = sheet_df('Process_Metrics')
for c_ in ['Avg_Cycle_Time_Days','Target_Cycle_Time_Days','On_Time_Pct','Volume_Per_Month','Error_Rate_Pct']:
    pmx[c_] = pd.to_numeric(pmx[c_])
print("\n=== WORST ON-TIME PER DEPT ===")
w = pmx.loc[pmx.groupby('Department')['On_Time_Pct'].idxmin()]
print(w[['Department','Process_Name','Avg_Cycle_Time_Days','Target_Cycle_Time_Days','On_Time_Pct','Volume_Per_Month','Error_Rate_Pct']].to_string(index=False))
print("\nProcesses below 65% on-time:")
print(pmx[pmx['On_Time_Pct']<65][['Department','Process_Name','On_Time_Pct','Avg_Cycle_Time_Days','Target_Cycle_Time_Days']].to_string(index=False))
pmx['w'] = pmx['Volume_Per_Month']*pmx['Avg_Cycle_Time_Days']
print("\nVolume-weighted avg cycle time per dept:")
print((pmx.groupby('Department')['w'].sum()/pmx.groupby('Department')['Volume_Per_Month'].sum()).round(2).to_string())
print("\nProcesses meeting target:")
print((pmx.assign(met=pmx['On_Time_Pct']>=65).groupby('Department')['met'].mean()*100).round(1).to_string())
EOF", "description": "Analyze staffing, overtime, and process metrics workbook"}

import pandas as pd, openpyxl

wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('task_folder/Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx', data_only=True)
ss = pd.DataFrame(wb['Staffing_Summary'].values[1:], columns=wb['Staffing_Summary'].values[0])
ss[['Authorized_Positions','Filled_Positions','Vacancy_Rate_Pct','Avg_Tenure_Years','Turnover_Rate_Pct','Avg_Annual_Salary']] = ss[['Authorized_Positions','Filled_Positions','Vacancy_Rate_Pct','Avg_Tenure_Years','Turnover_Rate_Pct','Avg_Annual_Salary']].astype(float)

print("=== STAFFING SUMMARY ===")
tot_auth, tot_fill = ss['Authorized_Positions'].sum(), ss['Filled_Positions'].sum()
print(f"Total authorized: {tot_auth}, filled: {tot_fill}, vacancies: {tot_auth-tot_fill}, citywide vacancy: {100*(tot_auth-tot_fill)/tot_auth:.1f}%")
d = ss.groupby('Department').agg(auth=('Authorized_Positions','sum'), filled=('Filled_Positions','sum'), vac_rate=('Vacancy_Rate_Pct','mean'), turnover=('Turnover_Rate_Pct','mean'), salary=('Avg_Annual_Salary','mean'))
d['vac_calc'] = 100*(d['auth']-d['filled'])/d['auth']
print(d.round(1).to_string())

# OT by dept annual
mo = pd.DataFrame(wb['Monthly_Overtime'].values[1:], columns=wb['Monthly_Overtime'].values[0])
for c_ in ['Regular_Hours','Overtime_Hours','Overtime_Cost_USD','OT_as_Pct_of_Regular']:
    mo[c_] = pd.to_numeric(mo[c_])
print("\n=== OT ANNUAL BY DEPT ===")
ot = mo.groupby('Department').agg(reg=('Regular_Hours','sum'), ot_h=('Overtime_Hours','sum'), ot_cost=('Overtime_Cost_USD','sum'), avg_pct=('OT_as_Pct_of_Regular','mean'))
ot['pct_calc'] = 100*ot['ot_h']/ot['reg']
ot['avg_hr_rate'] = ot['ot_cost']/ot['ot_h']
print(ot.round(2).to_string())
print("\nTotal OT cost:", ot['ot_cost'].sum().round(0), " Total reg hours:", ot['reg'].sum(), " Total OT hrs:", ot['ot_h'].sum())
print("\nOT pct by month x dept:")
pm = mo.pivot_table(index='Month', columns='Department', values='OT_as_Pct_of_Regular', aggfunc='mean')
print(pm.round(1).to_string())

# Process metrics: worst on-time per dept
pmx = pd.DataFrame(wb['Process_Metrics'].values[1:], columns=wb['Process_Metrics'].values[0])
for c_ in ['Avg_Cycle_Time_Days','Target_Cycle_Time_Days','On_Time_Pct','Volume_Per_Month','Error_Rate_Pct']:
    pmx[c_] = pd.to_numeric(pmx[c_])
print("\n=== PROCESS METRICS: worst on-time per dept ===")
w = pmx.loc[pmx.groupby('Department')['On_Time_Pct'].idxmin()]
print(w[['Department','Process_Name','Avg_Cycle_Time_Days','Target_Cycle_Time_Days','On_Time_Pct','Volume_Per_Month','Error_Rate_Pct']].to_string(index=False))
print("\nProcesses below 65% on-time:")
print(pmx[pmx['On_Time_Pct']<65][['Department','Process_Name','On_Time_Pct','Avg_Cycle_Time_Days','Target_Cycle_Time_Days']].to_string(index=False))
# weighted avg cycle time per dept (volume weighted)

[{"content": ""You are a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield, where the five departments under review total 596 authorized positions (542 filled): Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, and Fire Department. The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

Local Reference Files:
- Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv
- Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx
- NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv


External reference snapshots are provided in task_folder/references/ when the task requires external sources. Use these pinned files; internet access is unavailable. Write requested deliverables in /work/output/.

[{"content": ""You are a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield, where the five departments under review total 596 authorized positions (542 filled): Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, and Fire Department. The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.

Local Reference Files:
- Greenfield_311_Service_Requests_FY2024.csv
- Greenfield_Dept_Staffing_Overtime_FY2024.xlsx
- NYC_Expense_Budget_Selected.csv


External reference snapshots are provided in task_folder/references/ when the task requires external sources. Use these pinned files; internet access is unavailable. Write requested deliverables in /work/output/.

[{"content": ""You are a Management Analyst at the City of Greenfield, where the five departments under review total 596 authorized positions (542 filled): Parks & Recreation, Sanitation, Transportation, Health Services, and Fire Department. The City Council will vote on a departmental restructuring proposal, and you must prepare the decision package.

Proposal A (\"Consolidate\") would merge Health Services and Parks & Recreation into \"Community Wellness\" and merge Transportation and Sanitation into \"Public Works,\" with Fire remaining standalone — premised on shared fleet, field crews, and geographic route overlap. Proposal B (\"Targeted Fix\") would retain all five departments but impose cross-training pools, shared overtime budgets for departments exceeding 10% OT-to-regular-hours, and centralized hiring for divisions with vacancy rates above 12%.

Produce three deliverables using the provided data and any relevant NYC municipal benchmarks sourced separately — including the Mayor's Management Report performance indicators and the NYS Comptroller's analysis of post-pandemic city workforce trends.

The first deliverable is a Decision Briefing Memo (.docx, 6–10 pages) that opens with a situation overview cross-referencing staffing health against citizen service outcomes, followed by a comparative benchmark analysis contextualizing Greenfield's performance relative to NYC analogs. The memo must evaluate each proposal's impact on process bottlenecks, overtime cost structure, service delivery risk for underperforming SLAs, and workforce feasibility — then close with a clear recommendation (one proposal or a defined hybrid) backed by quantitative arguments and explicit assumptions.

The second deliverable is a Cost-Benefit Analysis Workbook (.xlsx) with four tabs. \"Baseline Metrics\" should present a department scorecard covering vacancy rate, OT percentage, average 311 resolution days, worst on-time process percentage, and Greenfield-vs-NYC per-employee budget ratio, with red conditional formatting applied where vacancy exceeds 12%, OT exceeds 10%, or on-time falls below 65%. \"Proposal A Model\" should project merged-department headcount, combined OT costs, and cycle times with documented assumptions for overlapping divisions and shared-fleet savings. \"Proposal B Model\" should show cross-training pool sizes, OT budget caps, and centralized hiring targets, identifying which divisions currently trigger each intervention. \"Comparison Summary\" should compare both proposals side-by-side on five dimensions — annual cost savings, FTE reallocation count, projected SLA improvement, implementation complexity (1–5), and risk rating (1–5) — with a net recommendation score.

The third deliverable is a Council Presentation (.pptx, 8–12 slides) summarizing current operational health, the trade-offs between proposals in table or chart form, NYC benchmark context, and a recommendation with next steps.

All quantitative claims must be internally consistent across all three deliverables and traceable to source data.

The NYC benchmark analysis should incorporate the externally sourced Mayor's Management Report (MMR) agency performance indicators (NYC Open Data dataset rbed-zzin) for DPR, DSNY, DOT, DOHMH, and FDNY — focusing on service-level agreement metrics and response time targets — and the NYS Comptroller's \"2024 Update on New York City Staffing Trends\" (Report 2-2025), covering post-pandemic vacancy rates, agency-level attrition, and overtime spending growth.
